page: Amazon Web Services m7a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance exposes 192 dedicated physical cores running at 3.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, providing 192 total vCPUs. It features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware instruction support for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and secure virtualization extensions. Memory capacity totals 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded compute capability and high memory bandwidth. In stress-ng multi-core tests, the system placed in the top tier with a score of 592,966.54, complemented by a Geekbench multi-core rating of 20,637.0 and high scores in Clang compilation and ray tracing. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 657.74 GB/sec read and 314.43 GB/sec write. In-memory transaction throughput is highlighted by 331.8 million Redis SET operations per second, while network serving achieves 113.03 GB/sec over its 50 Gbps baseline interface.

Architectural tradeoffs center on storage and accelerator profiles. The m7a.metal-48xl includes no bundled local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs, meaning persistent storage and acceleration must rely on network-attached volumes or external systems. While CPU-based LLM prompt processing achieves top-tier throughput via AVX-512 instructions, sustained token generation for large parameter models remains average relative to GPU-equipped alternatives.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the platform delivers high compute density and throughput per socket by dedicating pure physical cores without hypervisor overhead. It is best suited for compute-heavy multi-threaded tasks, distributed compile pipelines, in-memory caching layers, high-volume static web serving, and enterprise container hosting.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose instance featuring 192 dedicated physical cores on AMD EPYC 9R14 processors clocked at 3.7 GHz. Configured with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz and a 50 Gbps baseline network interface, it delivers a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The server provides no integrated local disk storage and zero GPUs, requiring remote volumes for persistence. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier multi-threaded processing, exceptional memory bandwidth, and leading performance in Redis transactions and Clang compilation tasks. Advanced vector instruction sets including AVX-512 and BF16 accelerate numerical and inference workloads. Given its lack of virtualization overhead and dense non-hyperthreaded core layout, the instance is suitable for intensive CI/CD build farms, in-memory databases, web serving tiers, and multi-threaded analytical computation.
